title: Metrics collector: the cadences, the collectors of the catalogue, the baseline file and the publication into the fleet store

Policy.description: The authored numbers of the collector. `tickMilliseconds` is the cadence of the host gauges (the finest bucket of tier t0), `slowMilliseconds` the cadence of the counter files and status files and of the fleet-scope collectors. `baselineMaximumAgeMilliseconds`: a persisted counter baseline older than this is only a new baseline (a long downtime is not one huge delta). `publishMilliseconds`: how often the publisher looks for rows closed since its last look; it appends exactly those rows (a few KB) in place to the published ring files, whose rows carry a start stamp at both ends, so a reader never takes a torn row, and the header cursor is written last; a whole file is copied (kernel copy, temporary name, rename) only when the published file is absent or of another layout. `fleetDirectory`: the directory below the store `v1/` that holds the fleet-scope rings `fleet/metrics/<source>/`. `fileBytesMaximum` bounds one published file. `lockFile` makes one collector the writer of a ring directory; `wardenFreshMilliseconds` is how old a warden state may be; `repoCpuMaximumGapMilliseconds` is the longest span between two warden readings that still gives a repo CPU rate.

Collectors.description: One entry per feeding collector: its cadence, the catalogue `source` of its metrics and the metric ids it feeds. Every catalogue id belongs to exactly one collector (a law test proves it, and that the source of each id is the source of its collector).

Unsourced.description: The ids whose collector has no source at all. Empty: every catalogue metric has a source; the law test pins the list so it can only stay empty.

Enums.description: The numbers of the state metrics.

Baseline.description: `baseline.json` in the local ring directory: the last cumulative reading of every counter metric, so a restart of the collector (every code change restarts it) continues the deltas instead of losing the count since the last tick.

Lock.description: `collector.lock` in the local ring directory: the process that writes the rings (one writer per directory), named by its identity (`pid` and `startMs`, so a reused pid is no holder), the `role` it collects for (`origin` for the machine, `fleet:<source>` for a fleet-scope source) and the `checkout` it runs for. Only a real collector may hold the lock of the machine-wide ring directory: a claim whose checkout lies inside the temporary directory, a claim made under a test runner, or a role outside `lockRolePattern` is refused; a test uses a private ring directory.
